meta.project: Document-Aware, Bilingual, and Explainable ESG-ABSA Intelligence System
meta.description: A structured mapping of the 5-layer integrated research plan to the curated literature corpus, establishing causal traceability from technical contributions to empirical evidence.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: xGQA: Cross-Lingual Visual Question Answering
literature_references.relevance: Provides empirical evidence on the difficulty of zero-shot cross-lingual transfer, justifying the need for the bilingual optimization proposed in RQ1.1 and C3.

literature_references.title: Improving Zero-shot Cross-lingual Transfer between Closely Related Languages by injecting Character-level Noise
literature_references.relevance: Supports C3 by demonstrating how character-level noise improves transfer between related varieties, applicable to regional calibration in ESG lexicons (RQ1.3).

literature_references.title: XFUND: A Benchmark Dataset for Multilingual Visually Rich Form Understanding
literature_references.relevance: Establishes a baseline for multilingual document understanding across diverse scripts, providing a structural precedent for the normalized ESG schema in C2.

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?

literature_references.title: Learning to Robustly Aggregate Labeling Functions for Semi-supervised Data Programming
literature_references.relevance: Directly supports C16 by proposing a framework for semi-supervised data programming to mitigate label scarcity in ESG datasets.

literature_references.title: Cutting Down on Prompts and Parameters: Simple Few-Shot Learning with Language Models
literature_references.relevance: Validates the few-shot approach in RQ2.1 by showing that fine-tuning only bias terms can achieve high accuracy with minimal parameter updates.

literature_references.title: FocusLLM: Precise Understanding of Long Context by Dynamic Condensing
literature_references.relevance: Provides the technical foundation for the long-context architecture in C13, utilizing dynamic condensing to integrate extensive sequences up to 400K tokens.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?

literature_references.title: Towards Collaborative Neural-Symbolic Graph Semantic Parsing via Uncertainty
literature_references.relevance: Establishes the causal link for C7 and RQ3.1 by demonstrating how symbolic knowledge improves neural parser performance in long-tail scenarios.

literature_references.title: Agentic Reasoning: A Streamlined Framework for Enhancing LLM Reasoning with Agentic Tools
literature_references.relevance: Supports C7 by introducing Mind-Map agents that use structured knowledge graphs to maintain coherence in long reasoning chains.

literature_references.title: GAMEBoT: Transparent Assessment of LLM Reasoning in Games
literature_references.relevance: Direct evidence for RQ3.2, utilizing rule-based algorithms to validate intermediate reasoning steps for transparent output assessment.

research_questions: RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?
RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?

literature_references.title: Mitigating Contradictions in Dialogue Based on Contrastive Learning
literature_references.relevance: Provides a methodology for greenwashing detection (C11) by discriminating contradictory patterns through contrastive learning.

literature_references.title: ICR Probe: Tracking Hidden State Dynamics for Reliable Hallucination Detection in LLMs
literature_references.relevance: Justifies RQ4.5 by introducing the ICR Score to differentiate factual evidence from hallucinated commitments in narrative disclosures.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: AXIS: Efficient Human-Agent-Computer Interaction with API-First LLM-Based Agents
literature_references.relevance: Enables the deployment goals of C12 and RQ5.2 by reducing latency and increasing reliability in agent-human interactions through API prioritization.

literature_references.title: A Simple Hash-Based Early Exiting Approach For Language Understanding and Generation
literature_references.relevance: Supports the scalability requirements in RQ5.2 by providing a lightweight method to achieve higher inference speed with fewer FLOPs.
